sections.h2: What are my options for selling an East Point house?
sections.html:
An East Point owner has three exits: put the house on the market through an agent, run the sale personally, or hand the keys to an investor who pays cash. Each exit trades money against effort, and the house's condition usually tips the scale.

The agent route gets the best shot at full price when the roof is sound and the rooms show well, though a buyer's lender and inspector control the calendar. Running the sale yourself removes the commission and adds a long list of chores. An investor writes one check for the house in whatever shape it is in, and the discount from retail pays for the speed.

  • Agent listing: widest audience, slowest to a firm closing date.
  • Personal sale: more profit retained, more work retained too.
  • Investor purchase: shortest path to closing, shaved price.

Before any conversation, set the deed, the current East Point city bill, the Fulton County bill and your payoff letter side by side. Those four papers answer most of what a title attorney asks in the first call.

sections.h2: How does East Point's housing profile look in federal data?
sections.html:
The July 2025 federal estimate puts East Point at 38,225 people, and renters outnumber owners: only 43.6 percent of homes were lived in by their owners across 2020-2024.

A renter majority shapes who answers a listing. Landlords and small investors are regular bidders here, and a tenant-occupied house is an ordinary thing to sell. If tenants live in yours, find the lease end date and the deposit amount first, since any buyer will ask for both. The midpoint value also hides a wide spread between the bungalows near downtown and the larger ranch lots farther out.

sections.h2: Why do buyers look at East Point?
sections.html:
Buyers look at East Point for the location. The city's own profile says it began as the eastern end of the Atlanta & West Point Railroad, started with 16 families in 1870 and received its charter in 1887. Today it calls itself five minutes from Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport and ten minutes from downtown Atlanta.

The profile counts more than 25 neighborhoods. Around the historic downtown, it describes tree-lined, walkable streets with bungalows, cottages and Cape Cod houses. Moving outward, it describes larger brick ranches with bigger yards, privacy, garages or basements, and some newer construction. MARTA bus and rail serve the city, and the city notes the traffic is light.

  • Camp Creek Marketplace has more than a million square feet of commercial and retail space.
  • Camp Creek Business Center and South Meadow Business Park supply nearby jobs.
  • Sumner Park holds a velodrome the city says is the only one in the state.
  • Annual downtown events include the Taste of East Point and a Fourth of July fireworks celebration.

Pick the lines that fit your street. A buyer from farther out will react to the airport and MARTA distances, while a buyer who wants a porch and a walk to dinner cares about the downtown blocks.

sections.h2: Who bills the property tax on an East Point house?
sections.html:
Two governments bill an East Point house separately: the City of East Point and Fulton County. The city's Finance Department collects city tax and runs city homestead exemptions, while valuations come from the Fulton County Board of Assessors and the city council sets the city millage rate.

The city's tax year follows the calendar, statements are generally mailed in the fall, and the due date, 60 days after mailing, appears on each statement. The state also approved a one-time 2026 Homeowner Tax Relief Grant that lowers assessed taxable value by up to $18,000 for homes with an approved homestead exemption. East Point says the credit posts to the city bill without a separate application, and it excludes rental, commercial and personal property.

Fulton County mailed 2026 Notices of Assessment in June. Owners could appeal the value within 45 days, and for most that window closed on July 31, 2026. In October 2026 the county commissioners held the general fund rate at 8.87 mills, its fifth straight year without a change.

  • City bill, payment and city exemption: East Point Finance.
  • Value, exemption records and appeals: Fulton County assessors.
  • Dividing this year's taxes with the buyer: your closing attorney.

sections.h2: What happens to a short-term rental permit when the house is sold?
sections.html:
Ask the Planning and Community Development Department whether a short-term rental permit carries over to a new owner before you promise a buyer anything. The city requires its permit before any listing appears on Airbnb or VRBO, and it renews each year.

The city treats a rental of 29 days or less as short term. It lists a $75 homestay license and a $150 whole-house lodging license, and it collects an 8 percent hotel/motel tax, with each month's tax due on the 20th of the next. Whole-house rentals are limited to a short list of zoning districts, including R1A, R-2, R-3, R-4, R-T and CR. East Point reported 65 permitted short-term rentals in 2025. Ordinance violations draw fines of $50 to $1,000 per offense, and every day a violation continues can count again.

If you operated a rental, gather your permit, your tax filings and any complaint history. Whoever buys will want proof that the address is in good standing.

sections.h2: What does Georgia add at the closing table?
sections.html:
Georgia taxes the transfer itself, and the tax has to be paid before a deed can be recorded. The sales contract names who covers it.

State law puts the liability on the seller, and plenty of contracts hand it to the buyer. A declaration form, PT-61, goes in electronically at closing. Questions about exemptions go to the clerk of superior court for Fulton County.

Ask the closing attorney for an itemized seller statement ahead of time. It should list your mortgage payoff, the prorated city and county taxes, the transfer tax if it is yours, and any balances the city shows against the address.

sections.h2: Which East Point situations favor an investor offer?
sections.html:
An investor offer helps most when delay is costing you. In East Point that usually means a house that sat vacant after an inheritance, a rental whose tenant stopped paying, a short-term rental you no longer want to operate, or a house needing repairs that a mortgage lender's appraiser would flag.

  • You want to name the closing day yourself.
  • The roof, plumbing or foundation needs work you will not finance.
  • You live out of state or are settling an estate from a distance.

Weigh any offer against what a repaired listing might net after commission and repair bills. Get the number in writing, see which closing costs fall on you, and treat the right to refuse as non-negotiable.

faqs.q: Does a Georgia seller have to fix East Point house problems before a cash sale?
faqs.a: No repair is required for a cash buyer who agrees to take the house in its present state. A buyer who uses a mortgage may negotiate repairs after the inspection or appraisal.

faqs.q: Who is liable for the real estate transfer tax on an East Point sale?
faqs.a: The seller carries it by default under state law, yet contracts often assign it to the buyer. Payment comes before recording of the deed.

faqs.q: Where do I look up an East Point property tax account?
faqs.a: Use the Property Tax Search on the City of East Point site for the city bill and the Fulton County Tax Commissioner for the county bill. Assessment notices and exemption records are at fultonassessor.org.

faqs.q: Will the 2026 Homeowner Tax Relief Grant reduce tax on my rental house?
faqs.a: No. East Point's finance page limits the grant to homeowners with an approved 2026 homestead exemption. It posts as a credit on the city bill, and it does not apply to rental property.

faqs.q: Is it a problem to sell an East Point house while tenants live there?
faqs.a: It is common. With 43.6 percent of homes owner occupied, East Point has many rentals. Review the lease and deposit, and tell every prospective buyer that the unit is occupied.
